title: Scalar closure and normalized comparison limit image
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extensions $E,L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, composable scheme morphisms $Z\xrightarrow{h}X\xrightarrow{f}Y$ with $\ell$ invertible at every point, three constructible derived-complete integral objects $M_i$ on $Y$, arbitrary flat-term K-flat representatives $P_i$, and isomorphisms $Q(P_i)\cong M_i$. Use the exact quotient complexes, finite expressions, substitutions and transports of [def-pur-completed-comparison-quotient-realization-data]. Fix also $\iota:E\to L$. For any GoodExpressions and invertibility proofs for the E substitutions, every ScalarGenerated expression is ScalarGood, and ScalarLimitImage holds: there are normalized L Roos/scalar models and invertible recursive L substitutions; the two actual strict scalar routes are equal; their limit image is the prescribed canonical L comparison; and each route yields both specified completed scalar/pullback/tensor composites.

source.place: Compatibility with finite reduction and extension of scalars; agent refinement of lem-pur-completed-comparison-quotient-realization, Scalar closure and normalized comparison limit image. Stacks 07A2, 0G7E, 07A4 and 0941.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-normalized-scalar-comparison-realization] to $E\subset L$ and $f$ (and to $h$ when needed). It gives the displayed balanced association $(x\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes i_n(a)b$, with insertion-of-one inverse, on the actual scalar quotient systems. It states that these and their pullback/tensor expressions are flat-term K-flat and normalized, retains every quotient transition, and identifies the canonical completed scalar comparisons $\alpha_F,\alpha_T$ with the limits of the strict scalar-association maps. This applies also when $L/E$ is ramified: it explicitly imposes no flatness on $B^E_{W,n}\to B^L_{W,n}$.

source.place: Integral level; scalar quotient models and the normalized realization of the fixed scalar comparisons (agent refinement).

proof.text:
Use [lem-pur-strict-coefficient-comparison-calculus] for the two quotient coefficient sequences $B^E_{W,\bullet}\to B^L_{W,\bullet}$ and the pro-etale inverse image of $f$. Its equation
$$c_L F_L(\sigma_Y)\kappa_{T_E}=T_L(\kappa_M,\kappa_N)\sigma_X S_X(c_E)$$
is an equality of strict chain-system maps: both routes have value $(b\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$ on $b\otimes(x\otimes y)$. It includes inverse, identity and successive-extension equations, with no coefficient-flatness hypothesis. Apply $\mathcal L_L$ and the normalized realizations of [lem-pur-normalized-scalar-comparison-realization]. The $\kappa,\sigma$ maps become $\alpha_F,\alpha_T$ by step 6; the $c_D$ maps become $\gamma_D$ by steps 2--3. Functoriality and cancellation of the intermediate realization isomorphisms give exactly the scalar equation in the statement. The same application to the inverse, identity and three-coefficient equations proves all their asserted compatibilities. Counit naturality as in step 4 retains their coherent reductions.

lean.statement:
theorem completedComparisonScalarLimitImage
    {Z X Y : Scheme.{u}} (h : Z ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [∀ z : Z, Invertible (l : Z.residueField z)]
    [∀ x : X, Invertible (l : X.residueField x)]
    [∀ y : Y, Invertible (l : Y.residueField y)]
    (M : Fin 3 → sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E Y)
    (P : Fin 3 → (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).FullSubcategory)
    (φ : ∀ i : Fin 3, DerivedCategory.Q.obj (P i).obj ≅ (M i).obj)
    (good : GoodExpressions l E h f P)
    (invertible : ∀ {W : Scheme.{u}} (A : StrictQuotient.Expression h f 3 W),
      IsIso (substitution l E P (fun i ↦ (M i).obj) φ good A)) :
    (∀ (d : Bool) (W : Scheme.{u}) (A : ScalarComplex l E L d W),
      ScalarGenerated l E L ι h f (fun i ↦ quotient l E (P i).obj) d W A →
        ScalarGood l E L d W A) ∧
    ScalarLimitImage l E L ι h f M P φ good invertible
